extraction.name: MATHVISTA
extraction.description: MATHVISTA is a benchmark designed to evaluate the mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visually complex scenarios. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). The benchmark covers seven types of mathematical reasoning (algebraic, arithmetic, geometry, logical, numeric commonsense, scientific, and statistical reasoning) and five primary tasks (figure question answering, geometry problem solving, math word problem, textbook question answering, and visual question answering). The dataset includes diverse visual contexts such as natural images, geometry diagrams, abstract scenes, synthetic scenes, charts, plots, scientific figures, tables, and more. MATHVISTA aims to bridge the gap in evaluating mathematical reasoning in visual contexts, which has been largely unexplored in existing benchmarks.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
extraction.citeAs: Lu, P., Bansal, H., Xia, T., Liu, J., Li, C., Hajishirzi, H., Cheng, H., Chang, K.-W., Galley, M., & Gao, J. (2024). MATHVISTA: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: MATHVISTA combines challenges from diverse mathematical and visual tasks, derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA). The data collection process involved: (1) Collecting nine MathQA datasets in multimodal settings, including four for geometry problem solving, two for math word problems with visual contexts, and two for textbook question answering on college curricula. (2) Reviewing over 70 datasets to select 19 that contain math-related instances, applying heuristic rules to automatically select examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning, followed by manual labeling by expert annotators to determine if they involve mathematical reasoning. (3) Creating three new datasets (IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA) to address gaps in logical reasoning on puzzle test figures, statistical reasoning on functional plots, and scientific reasoning on academic paper figures. All questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process to ensure data quality.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: MATHVISTA incorporates 28 existing multimodal datasets, including 9 math-targeted question answering datasets and 19 visual question answering datasets. The newly created datasets include IQTest (228 examples), FunctionQA (400 examples), and PaperQA (107 examples). The dataset covers diverse visual contexts such as natural images, geometry diagrams, abstract scenes, synthetic scenes, charts, plots, scientific figures, tables, and more.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The preprocessing steps included: (1) Automatic selection of mathematical problems using heuristic rules based on quantity words. (2) Manual labeling by expert annotators to determine if examples involve mathematical reasoning. (3) Rigorous review process to ensure data quality, with high inter-annotation consistency (99.2%). (4) Annotation of examples with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, and visual context. (5) Quality checks to address any unidentified errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Examples in MATHVISTA are annotated with metadata including question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, and visual context. The dataset features seven different types of mathematical reasoning abilities, with coarse labels of mathematical reasoning obtained from the details of the source datasets. Expert annotators manually label the mathematical reasoning categories for 1,000 examples to verify the quality of automatic annotation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation tool developed for manual labeling and refinement of examples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation process achieved high inter-annotation consistency with a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775, indicating substantial agreement among annotators. Among the newly collected 736 questions, only 6 exhibited disagreements in the annotated answers, which were resolved through discussion among the entire review team.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators were graduate students in STEM fields with expertise in mathematical reasoning and visual contexts. The annotation process involved three expert annotators for labeling mathematical problems and mathematical reasoning categories.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: EasyOCR for text detection in images, Multimodal Bard for generating image captions, and custom annotation tools for manual labeling and refinement.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is divided into two subsets: testmini (1,000 examples) for model development and test (5,141 examples) for standard evaluation. The answer labels for test will not be publicly released to prevent data contamination. An online evaluation platform is maintained for ongoing assessment. The dataset will be updated based on community feedback and evolving model capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MATHVISTA aims to bridge the gap in evaluating mathematical reasoning in visual contexts, which has been largely unexplored in existing benchmarks. The dataset is designed to push AI assistants towards general-purpose capabilities by combining mathematical and visual tasks, fostering advancements in AI models for real-world applications such as educational disciplines, logical queries about statistical data, and theorem proving.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential biases may arise from the selection of source datasets and the manual annotation process. The dataset includes diverse visual contexts and mathematical reasoning types, but the representation of certain types of mathematical problems and visuals may be limited. The annotations were sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations, and the heterogeneity of these sources may introduce inconsistencies in the annotation format and structure.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations include dataset coverage gaps, potential data noise, and the need for unified and comprehensive annotations. The dataset focuses on mathematical reasoning within visual contexts, spanning specific domains like science and college-level math, which necessitates a labor-intensive process for collecting high-quality data. The rapid development in foundation models may limit the comprehensiveness of the study. Future iterations aim to encompass a broader array of problems and visual contexts while providing unified and comprehensive annotations.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. MATHVISTA is designed to evaluate the mathematical reasoning capabilities of foundation models in visually complex scenarios. It serves as a benchmark for assessing the performance of models in tasks such as figure question answering, geometry problem solving, math word problems, textbook question answering, and visual question answering. The dataset is intended for use in developing and refining AI models for real-world applications involving mathematical reasoning in visual contexts.
